name: networkflowmonitor
description: Network Flow Monitor is a feature of Amazon CloudWatch Network Monitoring that provides visibility into the performance of network flows for your Amazon Web Services workloads, between instances in subnets, as well as to and from Amazon Web Services.

subcommands.name: create-monitor
subcommands.description: Create a monitor for specific network flows between local and remote resources, so that you can monitor network performance for one or several of your workloads.

subcommands.name: create-scope
subcommands.description: In Network Flow Monitor, you specify a scope for the service to generate metrics for.

subcommands.name: delete-monitor
subcommands.description: Deletes a monitor in Network Flow Monitor.

subcommands.name: delete-scope
subcommands.description: Deletes a scope that has been defined.

subcommands.name: get-monitor
subcommands.description: Gets information about a monitor in Network Flow Monitor based on a monitor name.

subcommands.name: get-query-results-monitor-top-contributors
subcommands.description: Return the data for a query with the Network Flow Monitor query interface.

subcommands.name: get-query-results-workload-insights-top-contributors
subcommands.description: Return the data for a query with the Network Flow Monitor query interface.

subcommands.name: get-query-results-workload-insights-top-contributors-data
subcommands.description: Return the data for a query with the Network Flow Monitor query interface.

subcommands.name: get-query-status-monitor-top-contributors
subcommands.description: Returns the current status of a query for the Network Flow Monitor query interface, for a specified query ID and monitor.

subcommands.name: get-query-status-workload-insights-top-contributors
subcommands.description: Return the data for a query with the Network Flow Monitor query interface.

subcommands.name: get-query-status-workload-insights-top-contributors-data
subcommands.description: Returns the current status of a query for the Network Flow Monitor query interface, for a specified query ID and monitor.

subcommands.name: get-scope
subcommands.description: Gets information about a scope, including the name, status, tags, and target details.

subcommands.name: list-monitors
subcommands.description: List all monitors in an account.

subcommands.name: list-scopes
subcommands.description: List all the scopes for an account.

subcommands.name: list-tags-for-resource
subcommands.description: Returns all the tags for a resource.

subcommands.name: start-query-monitor-top-contributors
subcommands.description: Create a query that you can use with the Network Flow Monitor query interface to return the top contributors for a monitor.

subcommands.name: start-query-workload-insights-top-contributors
subcommands.description: Create a query with the Network Flow Monitor query interface that you can run to return workload insights top contributors.

subcommands.name: start-query-workload-insights-top-contributors-data
subcommands.description: Create a query with the Network Flow Monitor query interface that you can run to return data for workload insights top contributors.

subcommands.name: stop-query-monitor-top-contributors
subcommands.description: Stop a top contributors query for a monitor.

subcommands.name: stop-query-workload-insights-top-contributors
subcommands.description: Stop a top contributors query for workload insights.

subcommands.name: stop-query-workload-insights-top-contributors-data
subcommands.description: Stop a top contributors data query for workload insights.

subcommands.name: tag-resource
subcommands.description: Adds a tag to a resource.

subcommands.name: untag-resource
subcommands.description: Removes a tag from a resource.

subcommands.name: update-monitor
subcommands.description: Update a monitor to add or remove local or remote resources.

subcommands.name: update-scope
subcommands.description: Update a scope to add or remove resources that you want to be available for Network Flow Monitor to generate metrics for, when you have active agents on those resources sending metrics reports to the Network Flow Monitor backend.
